title: End-to-End Latency Profiling Traces - 2026-04-20
content:
Summary:

This doc contains the latest end-to-end latency profiling traces collected during regression runs on 2026-04-18 through 2026-04-19. The goal was to (1) validate recent kernel/kernel-scheduling changes, (2) measure p50/p95/p99 across representative production workloads, and (3) provide a per-stage breakdown to identify dominant bottlenecks.

Key findings (high level):
- Baseline p50/p95/p99 for short-chat workload (avg prompt len ~40 tokens) is 78ms / 230ms / 540ms.
- Model compute (GPU kernel time) remains the largest single contributor to mean token latency for cold KV-cache requests (~55-70% of time).
- For prefix-heavy queries with KV cache hits, end-to-end p50 drops to ~48ms and p95 to ~140ms - indicating caching is effective but still subject to serialization + network overheads.
- There are intermittent p99 spikes driven by request queuing and serialization stalls when the host-side CPU is saturated by RPC marshaling.

Test harness and environment:
- Date range: 2026-04-18 to 2026-04-19
- Cluster: dedicated-runtime-prod-sim-4 (4x A100-80GB, CUDA 12.2, 8 CPU cores reserved per GPU)
- Serving binary: serving-runtime v1.14.2 (kernel-scheduler patch applied)
- Workloads:
  * short-chat: 20k requests, prompt tokens median 40, gen tokens median 16, temperature 0.2
  * long-context: 8k requests, prompt tokens median 1024, gen tokens median 64, KV-cache warm=50%
  * embeddings-emb: 5k requests (batching/aggregation test)
- Sampling: full traces collected for 2k requests per workload using built-in tracing (trace-level=timing, stack=true)
- Instrumentation: per-stage timers for ingress, auth, routing, queuing, request-parsing, dispatch, kv-cache lookup, model-compile/kernels, model-run (GPU), postprocess, serialization, egress

Aggregate numbers (selected):
- Short-chat (cold KV-cache, 20k reqs): p50=78ms, p95=230ms, p99=540ms
- Short-chat (warm KV-cache hits, 8k reqs): p50=48ms, p95=140ms, p99=360ms
- Long-context (mixed kv, 8k reqs): p50=420ms, p95=980ms, p99=1.8s
- Embeddings (batch size 8 median): p50=32ms, p95=88ms, p99=210ms

Per-stage breakdown (median contributions, short-chat cold):
- Network ingress + TLS termination: 6-12ms (8%)
- Auth & routing (policy check + model lookup): 3-6ms (4%)
- Queuing (wait for GPU slot / batching window): median 10ms, but p99 up to 300ms (variable)
- Request parsing (JSON parse + proto conversion): 4-7ms (5%)
- KV-cache lookup (miss path): 2-6ms (3%)
- Model compile/kernels selection / warm-up: 8-20ms (10%) - spikes when model variant selection differs
- Model-run (GPU compute) : 40-65ms (55-70%)
- Postprocess (token filtering, detokenize): 3-6ms (4%)
- Serialization & egress (protobuf encode + socket write): 8-20ms (10%)

Example trace (short-chat cold KV miss, p95 sample):
- trace_id: rt-20260418-7f3a
- timeline:
  0ms: request received on ingress
  7ms: routing+auth complete
  12ms: queued (waited 98ms) -> queued is where this p95 sample spent the most time
  110ms: dispatched to GPU host process
  120ms: KV-cache miss resolved (fetch model prefix if needed)
  138ms: kernel selection & compile checks (~12ms)
  210ms: GPU compute start -> GPU time 68ms
  282ms: postprocess & serialize (~18ms)
  300ms: response sent

Observations from traces:
- The largest p95/p99 contributor in the sampled runs is queuing induced by bursty arrival patterns combined with conservative batching windows. Several p99 traces spend >200ms in queue.
- Host CPU saturation correlated with peaks in serialization times; when CPU steal >60% we see serialization/egress p95 climb by ~2x.
- Kernel selection spikes occur when incoming requests route between model variants (fp16 vs quantized) and the scheduler triggers a short recompile/selection penalty (~8-20ms).

Root-cause hypotheses:
1) Batching window policy is too conservative for bursty traffic patterns (we open batch windows for 10ms by default) - increases queue tail latency during spikes.
2) Host-side RPC marshaling and protobuf encode path is single-threaded/contended in the current worker model leading to serialization stalls under load.
3) Model variant switching + lazy kernel selection introduces per-request jitter on the critical path when less common variants are selected.

Immediate experiments run (results):
- Reduce batching window from 10ms -> 6ms for short-chat traffic: p95 reduced by ~18% on median run; p99 reduced by ~12% but overall throughput dropped ~2.5% (expected tradeoff).
- Move serialization to a dedicated CPU thread pool (4 threads): peak serialization p95 dropped from 20ms -> 9ms; overall p99 traces with CPU saturation reduced by ~35%.
- Pre-warm kernel selection for low-traffic variants during deployment rollout: reduced kernel-selection spikes from 12-20ms down to 1-3ms in warm runs.

Recommendations / action items:
1) Temporary: deploy serialization thread-pool change to canary (target 10% of serving capacity) to validate in production burst scenarios.
2) Medium-term: adaptive batching windows - auto-tune open-window based on observed arrival rate and queue depth (reduce tail latency during bursts while preserving throughput).
3) Short-term: pre-warm kernel selection for any model variant that sees >1% of traffic during the last 24h window; add a small penalty if variant count explodes to limit memory.
4) Long-term: move RPC marshaling into a zero-copy path where possible (gRPC proto-zero or binary framing) to reduce CPU cycles per request.
5) Monitoring: add a new p95 queue-wait metric per host and alert when it exceeds 80ms for >1 minute.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Need to quantify throughput impact (RPS) of adaptive batching under mixed workloads (short-chat + long-context).
- Evaluate impact of kernel pre-warm memory pressure at 1000s of variants (corner-case customers).
- Confirm whether TLS termination reconfiguration (offloading) would materially reduce ingress time in current infra.

Appendix: raw p50/p95/p99 table (selected snapshots)
- short-chat (cold): p50=78ms, p95=230ms, p99=540ms
- short-chat (warm-kv): p50=48ms, p95=140ms, p99=360ms
- long-context (mixed): p50=420ms, p95=980ms, p99=1800ms
- embeddings (batch 8): p50=32ms, p95=88ms, p99=210ms

Notes: full trace bundles and timing histograms are uploaded to the artifacts bucket and linked in linked_artifacts above (CONFLUENCE-RT/latency-playbook references the histogram dashboard and raw traces).
